comment.comment:
The $OMNI thesis gets interesting when you ask one question: how much of your financial life do you actually want strangers watching?
CT celebrates wallet trackers until their own wallet becomes the entertainment. Every buy gets copied. Every sell gets posted. Suddenly everyone has an opinion on your fucking money.

Omni is going straight at that problem. Its latest updates describe buying through fresh addresses, selling back into a private balance, and batching withdrawals to make timing harder to follow. That’s a clear reason for traders to try the product. (nitter.cf)

What makes me bullish is the potential for repeat use. A trader who values keeping one position private probably wants the same for their next ten. If the experience delivers, privacy can become a habit—and habits are where lasting product demand comes from.

That’s the opportunity I see with $OMNI. Win over people who already trade every day. Give them control over what they reveal. Keep making it easier.

Your trades. Your business. Let the timeline find something else to talk about.

comment.comment: This tech actually seems amazing. With privacy being the meta right now, there are many different competitors and interesting projects like Veil, Nullmask, etc. This is because privacy when it comes it to crypto has so many different angles. Each project focuses on one thing, like anonymous transactions, token launching, etc. Omni is attacking all the different aspects in one. It truly seems like the holy grail of security and privacy in crypto. That in itself is extremely valuable, but at the same time I think for the average crypto user it is hard for them to rely on many pieces of technology for different functionalities. Having everything centralized makes it much more ideal for the average user, which is what Omni is striving to provide. We're obviously very early, but if this starts getting adopted, the potential is insanely high. The community here is goated too.
